Questions about this Agenda? Should any person have a question concerning any of the above
Agenda items prior to the meeting, please contact the City Clerk in person or by telephone at (626)
308-2816 during regular office hours.

NOTE: CITY HALL IS AN ACCESSIBLE FACILITY PER THE AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT.

  A. RECOGNITION OF STATE CHAMPION FOR DRAMATIC INTERPRETATION

  GRADUATION
  D. UPPER SAN GABRIEL VALLEY MUNICIPAL WATER DISTRICT – STATE OF
  THE DISTRICT AND LOCAL WATER SUPPLY UPDATE

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. I
  will give you a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to me before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please state
  your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2019  2
   A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of June 4, 2019.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of June 4, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2019

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of May 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-21 APPROVING FISCAL YEAR 2019-20
  INVESTMENT POLICY

  California Government Code Section 53646 requires the annual review of the
  City’s Investment Policy at a regular meeting of the City Council. Historically,
  the Investment Policy has been approved as part of the Budget Adoption
  process; however, beginning this year, the Policy will be presented as a separate
  item for consideration.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-21 approving
  the fiscal year 2019-20 Investment Policy.

  E. CONSIDERATION OF REQUEST SUBMITTED BY ATHENS SERVICES FOR
  RATE ADJUSTMENT

  For many years, the City has contracted with Athens Services to provide
  residential and commercial waste disposal services to the residents and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2019  3
   businesses of San Gabriel. In accordance with Section 8.2 of the Contract, it is
  necessary for the Council to endorse all proposed annual rate adjustments,
  which may be submitted not more often than annually. The most recent rate
  schedule was adopted by the City Council in June 2018.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council endorse the annual rate adjustment
  proposed by Athens Services for its services not to exceed the attached rate
  schedule effective July 1, 2019.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 19-19 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE OF PASQUAL
  AVENUE, FROM SYCAMORE DRIVE TO THE NORTH END OF PASQUAL
  AVENUE ON JULY 4, 2019

  The Public Works Department received a request from Jeff Heller and Sherry
  Chung for a temporary street closure for a neighborhood block party on
  Thursday, July 4, 2019 from 2:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. of Pasqual Avenue, from
  Sycamore Drive to the north end of Pasqual Avenue. The street closure will
  enable the community members to congregate safely in a centralized location.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-19 authorizing
  closure of Pasqual Avenue, from Sycamore Drive to the north end of Pasqual
  Avenue from 2:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. on Thursday, July 4, 2019.

  G. RESOLUTION NO. 19-20 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE OF BRIDGE
  STREET, FROM SYCAMORE DRIVE TO THE NORTH END OF BRIDGE STREET
  ON JULY 6, 2019

  The Public Works Department received a request from Ray Abeyta for a
  temporary street closure for a neighborhood block party on Saturday, July 6,
  2019 from 4:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. of Bridge Street, from Sycamore Drive to the
  north end of Bridge Street. The street closure will enable the community
  members to congregate safely in a centralized location.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-20 authorizing
  closure of Bridge Street, from Sycamore Drive to the north end of Bridge Street
  from 4:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. on Saturday, July 6, 2019.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2019  4
   H. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR THE PUBLIC WORKS
  FACILITY STORM DRAIN CONNECTION TO RUBIO WASH PROJECT
  CONTRACT, NO. 19-04

  The storm drain connection to Rubio Wash Channel is the last project item of
  the original Public Works Facility construction project. The Public Works Facility
  construction was completed in 2015. However, due to the long-lead-time
  design and permit requirement process with the Los Angeles County Public
  Works (LACPW) and the United States Army Corps of Engineers, the permanent
  storm drain piping connection to Rubio Wash Channel could not be
  accomplished at the time of the completion of the Facility construction.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve plans and specifications for the Public Works Facility Storm Drain
  Connection to Rubio Wash Project, Contract No. 19-04; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute contract documents with Adjul
  Corporation DBA Lee Construction Company for total bid amount in the
  amount of $68,775.00; and
  3. Approve a Purchase Order in the amount of $75,652.50 which includes a
  10% construction contingency.

  I. REQUEST TO ACCEPT DONATIONS AND GRANTS AND INCREASE FISCAL
  YEAR 2018-19 BUDGET FOR COMMUNITY SERVICES AND MISSION
  PLAYHOUSE

  At various times throughout the year, Community Services and Mission
  Playhouse receive grants, donations and other sources of funds. These are often
  received for programs or events held within the departments. In order to accept
  the funds, have the appropriate revenue account reflect the increase in funds,
  and increase the expenditure budget, staff must take this item to the City
  Council for approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Accept the donations and grants received by Community Services and
  Mission Playhouse; and
  2. Authorize expenditure of Park Development Impact Fees in the amount of
  $10,852.63 to cover expenses of the new playground equipment for the
  KaBOOM! Project; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2019  5
   3. Appropriate $10,852.63 from Development Impact Fees into account #122-
  850-40-97-807 to cover the City’s portion of the playground and the
  additional playground component; and
  4. Increase corresponding expenditure accounts by the amount included in
  the staff report.

  J. PROCUREMENT OF PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT FOR VINCENT LUGO PARK

  Vincent Lugo Park is the city’s largest park and recreation resource. Recent
  construction improvements have enhanced the park’s open space. Phase 2 of
  the Vincent Lugo Park Renovation is included in the Capital Improvement
  Program and includes the design and installation of picnic shelters, the
  installation of outdoor fitness equipment which was funded in part by
  Greenfields Fitness, and the design and construction of a new playground. The
  installation of the picnic shelters and outdoor fitness equipment are complete.
  The final item for Phase 2 renovation is the design and construction of the
  playground.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive the formal purchasing policy and
  authorize the issuance of a purchase order with preferred vendor Miracle
  Recreation Equipment Company for the acquisition of Custom Miracle KC Play
  Equipment for Vincent Lugo Park in the amount of $181,882.43, including sales
  tax and delivery. The purchase is to be funded from account #122-850-40-97-
  907.

  K. RESOLUTION NO. 19-26 TO ADOPT AN INTERFUND LOAN POLICY

  Interfund loans involve the lending of cash from one City fund to another for a
  specific purpose with a requirement for repayment. The practice of interfund
  loans is a recognized and necessary aspect of municipal finance. The City’s
  auditor (White Nelson Diehl Evans LLP) recommended the addition of an
  interfund loan policy to ensure that these loans are properly approved.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-26 and
  Interfund Loan Policy as presented.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2019  6
   A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS APPROVING THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-20
  OPERATING BUDGET, CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM BUDGET,
  AMENDING THE 2018-19 BUDGET, AND ESTABLISHING THE 2019-20
  GANN APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT

  This year’s budget document has been reformatted to encompass the provision
  of the recently adopted Fiscal Sustainability Policy in an effort to increase
  transparency and readability of the information presented. It includes historical
  data for both revenue and expenditures at the line-item level for all General
  Fund sources and uses. Budget Study sessions were held on April 2, May 7, June
  4, and June 11, 2019 to discuss a variety of issues related to the budget and
  fiscal health of the City.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing on the 2019-
  20 Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budgets and after receiving
  comments and testimony adopt the following resolutions:
  1. Resolution No. 19-22 Amending the 2018-19 Budget;
  2. Resolution No. 19-23 Adopting the City of San Gabriel 2019-20 Operating
  Budget Exhibit A to Resolution;
  3. Resolution No. 19-24 Approving the City of San Gabriel 2019-20 to 2023-
  24 Five-Year Capital Improvement Program and Adopting the 2019-20
  Capital Improvement Program Budget;
  4. Resolution No. 19-25 Adopting the City of San Gabriel’s Appropriation Limit
  for the 2019-20 Fiscal Year.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PROJECT REVIEW: PACIFIC SQUARE MIXED-USE PROJECT (PLANNED
  DEVELOPMENT (PD), DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT (DA), TENTATIVE
  TRACT MAP (TTM), AND PRECISE PLAN OF DESIGN (PPD)) AT 700-800
  SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD
  PLANNING CASE NO. PD18-001
  APPLICANT: PACIFIC SQUARE SAN GABRIEL LLC

  The subject property is located on the east side of South San Gabriel Boulevard
  between East Grand Avenue (to the south) and East El Monte Street (to the
  north). The San Gabriel Nursery and Florist occupied the site from the mid-
  1920s until 2016. San Gabriel Nursery and Florist continues to operate just north
  of the project site on an approximately two-acre parcel. In 2018, following an
  act of arson where many of the greenhouses and related structures were

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2019  7
   damaged or destroyed, the project site was largely demolished; however, some
  building foundations, trees, and landscaping remain.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and file the staff report.

  B. MEMORANDUM  OF  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE DRUG
  ENFORCEMENT AGENCY AND SAN GABRIEL POLICE DEPARTMENT

  The City Council will consider a proposal to assign one San Gabriel Police Officer
  to the Drug Enforcement Agency’s Los Angeles High-Intensity Drug Trafficking
  Area task force. The purpose of this assignment is to attain additional resources
  for the proactive effort of curbing the criminal activity associated with illicit drug
  trade in San Gabriel and surrounding areas.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council assign one investigator to the Los
  Angeles High-Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) Task Force and entering
  into the Memorandum of Understanding with the Drug Enforcement Agency.
